skill.name: seo-new-keywords-research
skill.description: Turn new AI names or unstructured AI market signals into a keyword priority table. For each name it finds the generic search terms downstream of it, screens them for relevance, and checks novelty, demand size and momentum against Google Ads volume and Google Trends, ending in prioritize, watch or skip. Use when the user has new model, product or repository names (or an AI listening report, a batch of posts, a changelog) and asks which keywords to build pages or tools for. Runs the new-term-radar command line; needs an AISA_API_KEY, and a GOANYAPI_API_KEY improves it.
skill.summary: Guide new-term-radar research to prioritize emerging AI keywords using estimated demand, trends, and competition.
skill.author: zhuyansen

security_audit.summary: All 29 static findings reflect Markdown formatting, documented provider authentication, relevant links, or ordinary keyword analysis rather than the alleged threats. No evidence found of credential exfiltration or prompt injection in SKILL.md; the external CLI implementation was not provided for review. Separate workflow risks include executing an unpinned repository and initiating paid lookups after cost disclosure without explicit approval.

remediation.issue: The setup clones an unpinned repository before running its Python module.
remediation.suggestion: Require a reviewed commit or release and verify its integrity before execution. Obtain approval before installing or executing external code.

remediation.issue: The workflow discloses estimated costs but does not require explicit approval before paid API calls.
remediation.suggestion: Require approval of the selected names and estimated total unless an existing spending authorization applies. Set a maximum budget before execution.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned External Repository Execution
semantic_findings.description: Setup says to clone the repository 'if missing', then runs 'python -m radar keywords'. No reviewed commit or integrity check is required. This allows changing upstream code to execute with local credentials and filesystem access.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions directly connect an unpinned clone with module execution. The external implementation is unavailable, so this identifies supply-chain exposure, not proven malicious code.

semantic_findings.title: Paid Lookups Without Explicit Spending Approval
semantic_findings.description: Every lookup is paid, but the workflow says 'State the estimate, then' run the command. It does not require approval or a budget ceiling. An agent following these instructions could spend existing account credit without a separate spending authorization.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly describes paid calls and proceeds after disclosure, without an approval step. Existing user authorization could mitigate this workflow risk.

content.value_statement: New AI launches can attract brief attention without creating lasting search demand. This skill guides paid keyword research to separate launch spikes from broader opportunities.
actual_capabilities: Extract up to five specific AI model, product, tool, or repository names from supplied text.
Guide a batched new-term-radar CLI lookup with optional repository mappings.
Present named and generic keywords together, sorted into prioritize, watch, and skip decisions.
Explain estimated daily searches, novelty, momentum, trend geography, and available competition metrics.
Flag branded terms, missing optional credentials, failed sources, and weaker worldwide trend readings.
Summarize long-tail phrases, related names, and brief recommendations for pages or tools.
limitations: Requires a separately installed new-term-radar CLI and an AISA_API_KEY or existing AIsa CLI login; lookups are paid.
GOANYAPI_API_KEY is optional, but missing it reduces related-search evidence and country-specific trend coverage.
Daily search counts are approximate, and search volume data can lag by about two months.
The supplied skill contains instructions, not the CLI implementation; it cannot guarantee rankings, complete data, or trademark clearance.

prompt_templates.title: Research One Name
prompt_templates.prompt: Research keywords for [AI product name]. Show the estimated cost and ask for approval before paid calls. Explain the returned priority decision.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Names From Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: From these release notes, select up to five specific AI names: [text]. Explain exclusions and request cost approval before creating the keyword table.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: convert unstructured text into research targets.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Products And Repositories
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [names] using repository mappings [owner/repo pairs]. Request cost approval, batch the lookup, and highlight generic terms, brand flags, and competition.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: compare multiple candidates in one paid call.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Evidence Before Investment
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate [names] for page investment. Verify the CLI revision and request budget approval. Separate country-specific evidence from worldwide readings; report failures and recheck candidates.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess evidence quality before committing development work.

output_examples.input: Illustrative scenario: review SynthID Detector with a missing optional provider key.
output: The optional provider key is unavailable, so related-search evidence and country-specific readings may be limited.
A flat worldwide reading means no rise was seen, not that demand did not rise.
Use only returned keywords and estimates; do not invent missing rows.

output_examples.input: Illustrative scenario: interpret a returned keyword demoted because competition is crowded.
output: Reason: The keyword was rising, but crowded page-one results caused the radar to lower its priority.
Recheck after several days because early search results can change.

best_practices: Review and pin the external CLI revision before execution, then approve the estimated batch cost.
Provide specific names and repository mappings; keep each batch to five names or fewer.
Compare generic demand with name spikes, and retain geography, source failures, brand warnings, and estimate caveats.
anti_patterns: Treating a short launch spike as proof of lasting demand.
Presenting approximate daily searches as exact counts or recent volume data.
Interpreting missing sources or flat worldwide readings as proof that no opportunity exists.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Running research also requires the external CLI and provider credentials.

faq.question: Which credentials are required?
faq.answer: An AISA_API_KEY or existing AIsa CLI login is required. GOANYAPI_API_KEY is optional and improves related-search evidence and country-specific readings.

faq.question: How much does research cost?
faq.answer: The documented estimate is about USD 0.05 per name plus USD 0.09 per call. Confirm current pricing and approve spending before execution.

faq.question: How many names can I research at once?
faq.answer: The workflow selects up to five names and batches them into one call. It estimates 40 to 90 seconds per name.

faq.question: Are daily search counts exact?
faq.answer: No. Daily counts are approximate and useful mainly for scale comparisons. Underlying search volume data can lag by about two months.

faq.question: Does a flat trend mean no demand?
faq.answer: No. Worldwide readings can miss recent movement, especially without the optional key. The report should state that no rise was seen.
